newsitem.title: USA: Titanium Metals in welded tubing venture.
newsitem.headline: Titanium Metals in welded tubing venture.

text.p: Titanium Metals Corp said Wednesday it has agreed with Valinox Welded, a specialist in welded tubing products, to form a joint venture to own and operate the welded tubing businesses of both companies.

Valinox Welded will own 54 percent of the venture, to be called Valtimet, and Titanium Metals will own 46 percent. Titanium Metals said pro forma combined sales of the joint venture for 1996 were about $110 million.

Titanium Metals makes welded titanium tubing in Morristown, Tenn., and Toronto, Ohio. Valinox Welded makes welded tubing, principally stainless steel and titanium, in Les Laumes, France, and in China through its majority-controlled subsidiary, Changzhou Valinox Great Wall Welded Tube Ltd.

The pact calls for the venture to acquire Titanium Metals's facilities in Tennessee and France, Valinox's interest in the Chinese manufacturer and the equipment used in Titanium Metals's Ohio tubing operations. Titanium Metals said it will be the key supplier of titanium strip products to the venture.
The pact remains subject to regulatory and lender approvals and is expected to close in the second quarter 1997.
